title: The Lid That Finally Budged
scene: A jam jar refuses to open at breakfast. A rubber band finally helps, and the speaker laughs at the effort-to-reward ratio.
sceneJa: 日曜の朝、ジャムの瓶のふたがどうしても開かない。布巾でもだめだったが、輪ゴムを巻くとようやく開いた。苦労したわりにトーストは一瞬で食べ終わり、思わず苦笑いする。

chunks.en: I reached for a jar of jam
chunks.ja: ジャムの瓶に手を伸ばした
トーストにつけようと思って
確かにそうだったはずなのに
ふたは緩めに閉めておいたはずなのに
布巾を使ってみたけれど

chunks.en: and my toast was getting cold.
chunks.ja: トーストは冷めていった

chunks.en: I wrapped a rubber band around the lid

chunks.ja: 滑りにくくなったおかげで
ようやくふたが開いた

chunks.en: I spent five minutes opening the jar
chunks.ja: 瓶を開けるのに5分もかかったのに

chunks.en: and ten seconds eating my toast.
chunks.ja: トーストを食べるのは10秒だった
なぜだか、それでよしと思えた

questions.question: Which split keeps 'did the trick' as one meaning chunk?
options: The extra grip helped / and that did / the trick: the lid finally came loose.
The extra grip helped / and that did the trick / the lid finally came loose.
The extra grip / helped and that did / the trick: the lid finally came loose.
questions.explanation: 'Did the trick' is a complete expression meaning that a method worked. Keep it together.

questions.question: What does 'the lid wouldn't budge' mean?
options: The lid was completely stuck and did not move.
The lid fell off by itself.
The lid made a strange sound.
questions.explanation: 'Wouldn't budge' means it refused to move even when the speaker tried.

questions.question: Why say 'Somehow, that felt fair'?
options: To complain about the price of jam.
To explain a plan to return the jar.
To joke about spending far longer opening the jar than eating the toast.
questions.explanation: The dry humour comes from accepting five minutes of effort for ten seconds of breakfast.

speak: Imagine: you want breakfast but a container will not open. Read: notice frustration, a practical idea, and a small victory. Chunk: say 'wouldn't budge', 'getting nowhere', and 'did the trick' as complete units. Understand: distinguish something stuck, unsuccessful effort, and a successful fix. Check: answer the three questions. Speak (30 seconds): describe what wouldn't budge, what you tried first, why you were getting nowhere, and what finally did the trick. Final Read: read all six sentences aloud, stress 'wouldn't budge', pause after 'On second thought', and end with gentle dry amusement.
review: New: 'wouldn't budge'（びくともしない）, 'I was getting nowhere'（一向に進展しない）, 'that did the trick'（それでうまくいった）. Reuse 'I could've sworn' (Lesson 106) and 'On second thought' (Lesson 109) in a new kitchen setting. Compared Lessons 101–114: unlike recent laundry, books, film, sports, and festivals, this story concerns a stubborn object and an absurdly brief reward. Sources: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/budge ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/do-the-trick ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/get-nowhere
